renders._yaml:
- component: card
  title: Matched fragment ions
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of fragment ions matched to a peptide's spectrum, and the box shows the spread across peptides. It answers how well the spectra support their identifications.
    How to read: more matched ions mean a better-supported spectrum. A box pushed toward few ions holds identifications resting on little evidence, so read it with the score distribution.
  column: fragment_ions
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median ions per peptide, with their spread

- component: card
  title: Fragment mass error
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median absolute fragment mass error in ppm of a peptide's matched ions, and the box shows the spread across peptides. It answers how accurately the fragment masses match the theory.
    How to read: a small error that is similar across samples means a well calibrated instrument. A sample with a larger error points to a calibration drift.
    Note: mhcquant sets its fragment tolerance in daltons for the search (default 0.01), not in ppm, so no ppm cut-off is drawn.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/mhcquant/blob/3.2.0/nextflow_schema.json
  column: fragment_error_ppm
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median error, with its spread

- component: figure
  title: Fragment mass error by sample
  description: |-
    Each bar counts the peptides whose median absolute fragment error falls in a range, coloured by sample. It answers how the mass accuracy is distributed within and between samples.
    How to read: distributions that overlap mean comparable mass accuracy. A sample shifted to the right has a calibration problem and less reliable matches.
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: fragment_error_ppm
    color: sample
    labels:
      fragment_error_ppm: Median absolute fragment error (ppm)
      sample: Sample
      count: Peptides

- component: table
  title: Fragment ions per peptide
  description: |-
    Each row is one identified peptide, with its matched b, y and other fragment ions, the median absolute fragment error in ppm and the matched intensity. It answers the exact figures behind every tile.
    How to read: sort by matched ions to find the best and the weakest supported peptides.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: length_profile
  title: Peptide length profile
  description: |-
    Each curve is one sample: the share of its distinct peptides at each length. It answers what the length signature of the immunopeptidome is, which tells the class of molecule that presented the peptides.
    How to read: a sharp peak at 9 residues inside the shaded window is the expected class I signature, and class II ligands peak near 15 residues in the HLA Ligand Atlas. A broad shoulder of longer peptides points to class II presentation or to contamination.
    Lines and annotations: the shaded band is the peptide length window mhcquant keeps by default, 8 to 12 residues. It is the pipeline's setting, so it hides longer peptides unless the run widened it.
    Sources: https://github.com/nf-core/mhcquant/blob/3.2.0/nextflow_schema.json and https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33858848/
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Peptide length (residues)
    y_title: Share of the sample's peptides
    shaded_bands:
    - - 8
      - 12
      - mhcquant default length window
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: length
    y: fraction

- component: figure
  title: Peptides per length class
  description: |-
    Each bar is the count of distinct peptides of one length in one sample, coloured by sample. It answers how many peptides each length class holds.
    How to read: the tallest bar should be the 9-mer for a class I sample. Samples of different depth differ in height, so use the profile above to compare shapes.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: length_class
    y: peptides
    color: sample
    barmode: group
    labels:
      length_class: Peptide length
      peptides: Distinct peptides
      sample: Sample

- component: interactive
  title: Peptide length
  description: Pick one or more peptide lengths to restrict the tiles to them. It answers what the table
    and the bars show for a single length.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: length_class

- component: table
  title: Peptide length counts
  description: |-
    Each row is one sample and peptide length, with the count of distinct peptides and their share of the sample. It answers the exact values behind the profile.
    How to read: filter by length class to compare samples at one length.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: motif_heatmap
  title: Amino-acid frequency by peptide position
  description: |-
    Each row is one position of the peptides of a given length in one sample, and each column an amino acid, coloured by the share of peptides carrying that residue there. It answers which residues the presented peptides favour at each position.
    How to read: columns that are dark at only a few positions are anchor residues, the signature of the presenting MHC allele. A flat, pale row has no preference, so little motif.
  kind: complex_heatmap
  config:
    cluster_rows: false
    cluster_cols: false
  roles:
    index: row_id
    value_columns:
    - A
    - C
    - D
    - E
    - F
    - G
    - H
    - I
    - K
    - L
    - M
    - N
    - P
    - Q
    - R
    - S
    - T
    - V
    - W
    - Y
    row_annotation_cols:
    - sample
    - length_class

- component: interactive
  title: Peptide length
  description: Pick one or more peptide lengths to restrict the heatmap and the table to them. It answers
    what the motif looks like for a single length.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: length_class

- component: table
  title: Positional amino-acid frequencies
  description: |-
    Each row is one position of one peptide length in one sample, with the number of peptides and the frequency of each amino acid. It answers the exact values behind the heatmap.
    How to read: filter by sample and length, then sort a residue column to find the position where it dominates.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: composition_bars
  title: Peptide composition per sample
  description: |-
    Each bar is one sample, stacked by the share of its distinct peptidoforms in each category of the chosen split: peptide length, precursor charge or modification state. It answers how the immunopeptidome is composed.
    How to read: switch the split to compare samples. Similar bars mean similar immunopeptidomes. A sample with an odd length or charge mix, or a high modified share, may reflect a different preparation.
  kind: stacked_bar
  config:
    value_title: Share of the sample's peptidoforms
    rank_label: Split by
  roles:
    sample_id: sample
    taxon: category
    rank: rank
    abundance: peptides

- component: table
  title: Peptide composition
  description: |-
    Each row is one sample, one split and one category, with the count of distinct peptidoforms. It answers the exact counts behind the bars.
    How to read: filter by split to read one composition at a time.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: rt_observed_predicted
  title: Observed against predicted retention time
  description: |-
    Each point is a peptide: its retention time predicted by DeepLC on the horizontal axis and the time observed in the run on the vertical axis, coloured by sample. It answers whether identifications behave as the prediction expects.
    How to read: points hugging the diagonal are consistent with the prediction. Points far off it are less trustworthy identifications, and a whole sample off the diagonal has a gradient or calibration difference.
    Lines and annotations: the diagonal is where observed equals predicted. It is an identity line, not a cut-off.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/mhcquant/blob/3.2.0/docs/output.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Predicted retention time (min)
    y_title: Observed retention time (min)
    reference_line: diagonal
    reference_label: Observed equals predicted
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    x: predicted_rt_min
    y: rt_min
    label: peptide
    color: sample

- component: advanced_viz
  id: rt_hydropathy
  title: Retention time against hydropathy
  description: |-
    Each point is a peptide: its hydropathy score (GRAVY, the mean hydropathy of its residues) on the horizontal axis and its observed retention time on the vertical axis, coloured by length class. It answers how retention relates to peptide hydrophobicity in each sample.
    How to read: compare samples and lengths. A sample whose cloud tilts differently from the others had a different gradient or column, so treat its retention times with care.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Hydropathy (GRAVY)
    y_title: Observed retention time (min)
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    x: gravy
    y: rt_min
    label: peptide
    color: length_class

- component: advanced_viz
  id: mz_retention
  title: Precursor m/z over the gradient
  description: |-
    Each point is a peptide: its observed retention time on the horizontal axis and its precursor m/z on the vertical axis, coloured by charge state. It answers how identifications spread over the gradient and the mass range.
    How to read: a gradient that is evenly populated is a healthy run. Gaps point to a segment of the run that identified little, and a charge state that dominates shows the mass range it covers.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Observed retention time (min)
    y_title: Precursor m/z
    top_n_labels: 0
  roles:
    x: rt_min
    y: mz
    label: peptide
    color: charge_state

- component: figure
  title: Peptide score by sample
  description: |-
    Each bar counts the peptides whose search-engine score falls in a range, coloured by sample. It answers how the identification scores are distributed.
    How to read: the score is the Comet XCorr in a quantified run, where higher is better. Samples whose distribution sits lower have weaker evidence, so read them with the fragment-ion tiles.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median search-engine score of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of mhcquant.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/mhcquant/blob/3.2.0/docs/output.md
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: score
    color: sample
    labels:
      score: Search-engine score
      sample: Sample
      count: Peptides
  reference_lines:
  - axis: x
    stat: median
    column: score

- component: card
  title: Peptide-spectrum matches
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total count of PSMs behind the peptides in view, and the bar splits it by modification state. It answers how much spectral evidence there is and how much of it is for modified peptides.
    How to read: a sum mixes samples, so read the median and the maximum beside it for a per-peptide reading.
  column: psms
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: modification_state
  caption: PSMs, by modification state

- component: card
  title: Distinct peptide sequences
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct peptide sequences, and the bar splits the rows by length class. The count of rows is also shown, since a sequence appears once per charge, modification and sample. It answers how many different peptides were found and at which lengths.
    How to read: for a class I sample the 9-mer segment should be the largest.
  column: sequence
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: length_class
  caption: distinct sequences, by length

- component: card
  title: Retention-time error
  description: |-
    The hero number is the range of the retention-time error (observed minus predicted) over the peptides in view, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how far observed times stray from the DeepLC prediction.
    How to read: a box tight around zero with a short range means the prediction fits. A box shifted off zero is a systematic offset, so check the gradient. The range is shown instead of the median because errors in both directions cancel.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/mhcquant/blob/3.2.0/docs/output.md
  column: rt_error_min
  aggregation: range
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: spread of the error, with its quartiles

- component: interactive
  title: Peptide length
  description: Pick one or more peptide lengths to restrict every tile to them. It answers what the plots
    show for a single length.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: length_class

- component: interactive
  title: Peptide score
  description: Drag the range to keep peptides with a score inside it. It answers how the plots change when
    only the best scored, or the weakest, peptides are kept.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: score

- component: table
  title: Identified peptides
  description: |-
    Each row is a peptide precursor in one sample, with its score, PSM count, retention times, m/z, charge, anchors, source proteins and intensity. It answers the exact detail behind every tile and lets a row selection filter the dashboard.
    How to read: select a sequence to see it across samples, or sort by score to inspect the best supported peptides.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: sequence

- component: advanced_viz
  id: replicate_upset
  title: Peptides shared between replicates
  description: |-
    Each bar counts the peptidoforms seen in one exact combination of replicates of a sample, and the dots below show which replicates are in it. It answers how much of a sample is seen in every injection.
    How to read: a tall bar for all replicates together means a reproducible sample. Tall bars for single replicates mean peptides seen only once, which are the least certain.
  kind: upset_plot
  config:
    color_intersections_by: degree
    show_values: true

- component: card
  title: Replicates a peptide is seen in
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average count of replicates in which a peptidoform is detected, and the histogram shows how many peptidoforms are seen in each count. It answers how consistently peptides are re-detected.
    How to read: a histogram piled at the highest count means most peptides are found in every replicate. A pile at 1 means many are seen once.
  column: replicates_detected
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: peptides, by replicates seen

- component: table
  title: Replicate detection per peptide
  description: |-
    Each row is a peptidoform in one sample, with a 0 or 1 for each replicate and the number of replicates it was detected in. It answers which peptides are missing from which replicate.
    How to read: filter to a count of 1 to list the peptides seen only once.

- component: figure
  title: Peptide intensity per replicate
  description: |-
    Each box is the distribution of peptide intensities in one replicate of a sample, on a log10 scale, coloured by sample. It answers whether the replicates of a sample were measured at comparable intensity.
    How to read: boxes at similar heights mean a consistent injection amount and sensitivity. A replicate shifted down or up has a loading or sensitivity difference, so treat its intensities with care.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median log10 peptide intensity of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of mhcquant.
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: replicate_label
    y: log10_intensity
    color: sample
    labels:
      replicate_label: Replicate
      log10_intensity: Log10 intensity
      sample: Sample
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: log10_intensity

- component: card
  title: Peptide detections
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of peptide detections over all replicates in view, and the bar splits it by replicate. The average beside it is the share of peptide and replicate pairs in which the peptide was detected. It answers how evenly the replicates contribute detections.
    How to read: equal segments mean replicates detect about as many peptides. A small segment is a replicate that detected fewer.
  column: detected
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - average
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: replicate_label
  caption: detections, split by replicate

- component: table
  title: Peptide intensity per replicate
  description: |-
    Each row is a peptide in one replicate of a sample, with whether it was detected and its log10 intensity. It answers the exact values behind the boxes.
    How to read: filter to a peptide to compare its intensity across replicates.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: replicate_scatter
  title: Intensity agreement between replicates
  description: |-
    Each point is a peptide quantified in two replicates of a sample: its log10 intensity in the first on the horizontal axis and in the second on the vertical axis, coloured by replicate pair. It answers how reproducible the quantification is.
    How to read: a pair that hugs the diagonal is reproducible. A wide cloud or a cloud shifted off the diagonal has noisy or biased intensities, so check the replicate correlation card before comparing samples.
    Lines and annotations: the diagonal is where the two replicates have equal intensity. It is an identity line, not a cut-off.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Log10 intensity, first replicate
    y_title: Log10 intensity, second replicate
    reference_line: diagonal
    reference_label: Equal intensity
    top_n_labels: 0
  roles:
    x: intensity_a
    y: intensity_b
    label: peptide
    color: pair

- component: interactive
  title: Replicate pair
  description: Pick one or more replicate pairs to restrict the scatter and the table to them. It answers
    how a single pair agrees.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: pair

- component: table
  title: Replicate intensity pairs
  description: |-
    Each row is a peptide in one replicate pair of a sample, with its log10 intensity in each replicate. It answers the exact values behind the scatter.
    How to read: sort by the difference between the two columns to find the peptides that disagree most.

- component: card
  id: yield_psms
  title: Peptide-spectrum matches
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of PSMs per sample, and the box shows the spread across samples. It answers how much spectral evidence each sample gives.
    How to read: samples of the same design should give similar counts. A sample far below its peers had a low yield, so treat its comparisons with care.
  column: psms
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median PSMs, with their spread

- component: card
  id: yield_peptides
  title: Distinct peptides
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of distinct peptide sequences per sample, and the box shows the spread across samples. It answers how deep each immunopeptidome is.
    How to read: immunopeptidomes of a similar input amount give similar depth. An outlier sample is under or over sampled.
  column: peptides
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median peptides, with their spread

- component: card
  id: yield_peptides_total
  title: Total peptides
  description: |-
    The hero number is the sum of distinct peptides over the samples in view, and the histogram shows how samples distribute over peptide counts. It answers how many peptides the dataset holds and how even the samples are.
    How to read: a sum mixes samples, so read the minimum and the maximum beside it. A histogram with one far bar is a sample out of step with the rest.
  column: peptides
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: peptides per sample

- component: card
  id: yield_proteins
  title: Source proteins
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of source proteins per sample, and the box shows the spread across samples. It answers how many proteins contribute peptides to each sample.
    How to read: a sample with many peptides but few proteins is dominated by a few abundant sources. Compare with the peptide counts.
  column: proteins
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median proteins, with their spread

- component: card
  id: modified_share
  title: Modified peptide share
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of a sample's peptidoforms that carry a modification, and the box shows the spread across samples. It answers how much of the immunopeptidome is modified.
    How to read: samples prepared the same way give similar shares. A sample with a much higher share may reflect a preparation artefact such as oxidation.
  column: modified_fraction
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median share, with its spread

- component: card
  id: ninemer_share
  title: 9-mer share
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of a sample's peptides that are 9 residues long, and the box shows the spread across samples. It answers how strong the 9-mer signature is.
    How to read: a class I immunopeptidome is dominated by 9-mers, so a low share points to a mix of classes or to contamination.
  column: ninemer_fraction
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median share, with its spread

- component: card
  id: class_i_share
  title: Peptides in the class I window
  description: |-
    The hero number is the lowest share of a sample's peptides that fall in the class I length window, 8 to 12 residues, and the median sits beside it. It answers whether any sample leaves the window.
    How to read: mhcquant keeps peptides of 8 to 12 residues by default, so the share is 1 unless the run widened the range. A lower share means the run kept longer peptides.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/mhcquant/blob/3.2.0/nextflow_schema.json
  column: class_i_fraction
  aggregation: min
  aggregations:
  - median
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: lowest sample, with the median

- component: card
  id: class_ii_share
  title: Peptides in the class II window
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest share of a sample's peptides that fall in the class II length window, 13 to 25 residues, and the median sits beside it. It answers whether any sample holds long peptides.
    How to read: with mhcquant's default length filter of 8 to 12 residues the share is 0, so a value above 0 means the run widened the range and the sample holds class II length peptides.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/mhcquant/blob/3.2.0/nextflow_schema.json
  column: class_ii_fraction
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: highest sample, with the median

- component: card
  id: median_length
  title: Median peptide length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean over samples of each sample's median peptide length, with the lowest and highest sample beside it. It answers how long the peptides are overall.
    How to read: samples of one class give about the same value. A sample with a clearly longer median holds longer peptides, so read it with the length profile.
  column: median_length
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: mean of sample medians, with the lowest and highest

- component: card
  id: replicate_correlation
  title: Replicate correlation
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over samples of the median Pearson correlation between replicate intensities, and the box shows the spread across samples. It answers how reproducible the quantification is.
    How to read: values close to 1 mean replicates agree. A low value means noisy intensities, so open the replicate scatter before trusting the quantities.
    Note: the correlation needs enough peptides quantified in both replicates, and samples without replicates have none.
  column: replicate_median_r
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median Pearson r, with its spread

- component: card
  id: replicate_worst_pair
  title: Weakest replicate pair
  description: |-
    The hero number is the lowest Pearson correlation between replicate intensities over the samples in view, and the box shows the spread of each sample's weakest pair. It answers whether any replicate disagrees with the others.
    How to read: a value much lower than the median correlation points to one bad replicate. Open its pair in the scatter.
  column: replicate_min_r
  aggregation: min
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: lowest r per sample, with its spread

- component: card
  id: replicate_completeness
  title: Peptides in every replicate
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of a sample's peptides that were quantified in every replicate, and the box shows the spread across samples. It answers how completely replicates agree on what is present.
    How to read: a high share means replicates detect the same peptides. A low share means many peptides are seen in one injection only.
  column: all_replicates_fraction
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median share, with its spread

- component: card
  id: rt_error
  title: Retention-time error
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over samples of each sample's median absolute retention-time error between observed and DeepLC-predicted time, and the box shows the spread. It answers how well the prediction fits each run.
    How to read: a small error that is similar across samples means a consistent gradient. A sample with a larger error had a different gradient or column.
  column: median_abs_rt_error_min
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median error, with its spread

- component: advanced_viz
  id: yield_vs_ninemer
  title: Depth against 9-mer share
  description: |-
    Each point is a sample: its distinct peptide count on the horizontal axis and its share of 9-mers on the vertical axis, sized by PSMs. It answers whether deeper samples keep the 9-mer signature.
    How to read: samples of one class cluster together. A point far from the others is a sample with a different depth or a different length mix, so open its length profile.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median share of 9-mers of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of mhcquant, which defines none.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Distinct peptides
    y_title: Share of 9-mers
    top_n_labels: 5
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: peptides
    y: ninemer_fraction
    label: sample
    size: psms

- component: table
  title: Immunopeptidome summary
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample, with its PSMs, peptides, proteins, modified share, length signature, median score, retention-time error and replicate statistics. It answers the exact figures behind every card and lets a row selection filter the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by a column to find the outlier samples, then select one to open it across the tiles.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: sample

- component: card
  title: Source proteins
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct source proteins, and the count beside it is the rows, one per sample and protein. It answers how many proteins give rise to the presented peptides and how many are shared between samples.
    How to read: a row count much higher than the distinct count means the same proteins are found in several samples. Shared peptides are credited to every protein they map to.
  column: protein
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: distinct proteins, with the sample and protein pairs

- component: card
  title: Peptides per source protein
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of distinct peptides per source protein, and the box shows the spread across proteins. It answers how many peptides a typical protein contributes.
    How to read: a few proteins with many peptides are the dominant sources. Open the scatter or the table to see which.
  column: peptides
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median peptides per protein, with their spread

- component: advanced_viz
  id: protein_coverage
  title: Source protein yield and intensity
  description: |-
    Each point is a source protein in one sample: its distinct peptides on the horizontal axis and its summed log10 intensity on the vertical axis, coloured by sample and sized by PSMs. It answers which proteins contribute the most peptides and signal.
    How to read: points toward the upper right are the dominant sources of the immunopeptidome. Proteins that dominate every sample are abundant cellular proteins, while sample-specific ones may reflect the biology under study.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Distinct peptides
    y_title: Summed log10 intensity
    top_n_labels: 8
  roles:
    x: peptides
    y: log10_intensity
    label: protein_entry
    color: sample
    size: psms

- component: table
  title: Source proteins
  description: |-
    Each row is a source protein in one sample, with its distinct and shared peptides, PSMs, best score, summed intensity and the peptides themselves. It answers the exact detail behind every tile and lets a row selection filter the dashboard.
    How to read: select a protein to see its peptides, or sort by peptides to find the dominant sources.
